studies.Title: Dietary beta-carotene and cancer of the prostate: a case-control study in Kyoto, Japan.
studies.Reference: Dietary beta-carotene and cancer of the prostate: a case-control study in Kyoto, Japan.
studies.Timing: Dietary interviews during hospital admission from 1981 to 1984
studies.Population: Hospital-admitted men with prostate cancer, benign prostatic hyperplasia, or other hospital conditions

extraction_supporting_text.cases: One hundred patients with prostate cancer and two different control series [100 benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) patients and 100 general hospital patients] were matched to each other upon hospital admittance, age (+/- 3 years) and date of admission (+/- 3 months), and directly interviewed during admission from 1981 to 1984 in Kyoto, Japan.
extraction_supporting_text.design: a case-control study in Kyoto, Japan
extraction_supporting_text.timing: directly interviewed during admission from 1981 to 1984
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: a quantitative food frequency technique for estimating usual diet

disease_scope_review.endpoint_excerpt: beta-Carotene as well as vitamin A contained in green/yellow vegetables were significantly protective, and those in seaweeds and kelp suggestively protective.
disease_scope_review.reason: Kelp-derived beta-carotene and vitamin A were evaluated as protective dietary factors in this general prostate cancer case-control study; no aggressive subtype is specified.

evidence_scope_projection.definition: Overall prostate cancer evidence, excluding estimates solely about aggressive prostate cancer. General estimates from papers that also report aggressive endpoints remain included. Uncertain endpoints retain their existing review and pooling restrictions.
